subject: mathematics
question_text: Solve for x: Tan⁻¹((x − 1)/(x − 2)) + Tan⁻¹((x + 1)/(x + 2)) = π/4.

mark_split.label: Take the tangent of both sides

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.115, chapter 10 INVERSE TRIGONOMETRIC FUNCTIONS, Short Answer question 8(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split is 1+1+1+1, with a whole mark reserved for testing the two roots, because taking the tangent of both sides is only a necessary condition and an untested root is a real loss of marks on this question type. NOTATION: the book prints the inverse functions in lower case (tan⁻¹); they are written here with capitals to match the principal-value convention used across the rest of this unit. Checked numerically to twelve decimal places: at x = +1/√2 and at x = −1/√2 the left side equals 0.785398163397 = π/4, and a scan of x over [−50, 50] found no other root. Replacing x by −x swaps the two fractions, so the left side is an even function of x and both roots stand. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, at 4 marks each, under the 2026-27 pattern; Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-only unit, so the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this one — name each move in order, and say how you test the roots you find.

steps.label: Name the two fractions
steps.margin_note: First mark. Naming the two fractions keeps the algebra short and makes the excluded values easy to see.
steps.memory_tip: Exclude x = 2 and x = −2 first — those two values make a denominator zero.

recall.must_convey: That the two fractions are named u and v and that x = 2 and x = −2 are excluded.
accept: call the first fraction u and the second v, and rule out x equals two and minus two
the denominators cannot be zero so x is not two or minus two
name the fractions before doing any algebra
x equals two and minus two ni exclude cheyyali
write the equation as tan inverse u plus tan inverse v equals pi by four
reject: take the tangent of both sides
the roots are plus and minus one over root two

steps.why: x = 2 and x = −2 must be excluded at the start, because the question's fractions have no value there.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to exclude x = 2 and x = −2.
Mixing up which fraction is u and which is v.

steps.label: Take the tangent of both sides
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both parts sit over x² − 4, so that factor cancels and the equation becomes a simple quadratic.
steps.memory_tip: Put u + v and 1 − uv over the same denominator x² − 4 — it cancels in the next line.

recall.must_convey: That the tangent of both sides is taken, giving (u + v)/(1 − uv) with both parts over x² − 4.
accept: take the tangent of both sides so the left becomes u plus v over one minus u v
u plus v is two x squared minus four over x squared minus four
one minus u v comes to minus three over x squared minus four
rendu parts x squared minus four meeda vasthayi
put both parts over the same denominator

steps.why: Taking the tangent of both sides turns the inverse equation into an algebraic one. Every solution of the original must satisfy it.
common_mistakes: Adding u and v without a common denominator.

steps.label: Solve the quadratic
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Both roots are only candidates at this stage, because taking the tangent of both sides can admit angles that differ by π.
steps.memory_tip: The x² − 4 cancels on the top and the bottom, leaving 2x² − 4 = −3.

recall.must_convey: That the equation reduces to 2x² − 4 = −3, giving x = ±1/√2 as candidates.
accept: since tan of pi by four is one the fraction equals one and x squared is a half
the x squared minus four cancels leaving two x squared minus four equals minus three
the candidates are plus and minus one over root two
x squared half, so x plus or minus one by root two
solve the quadratic to get the two candidate roots
reject: take the tangent of both sides
heard_as: tan pi by four is one

steps.why: The x² − 4 factors cancel, so the equation is a plain quadratic. Both signs of the square root stay candidates until they are tested.
common_mistakes: Keeping only the positive root without testing.
Cancelling x² − 4 while the excluded values still need it.

steps.label: Test both roots
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Replacing x by −x swaps u and v, so the left side has the same value at both roots and neither is rejected.
steps.memory_tip: Test each root in the original equation. The check is uv < 1 — if uv is not less than 1, the sum needs an extra π.

recall.must_convey: That both roots are put back in, uv = 1/7 < 1, and both satisfy the original equation.
accept: put both roots back in, u v is one seventh which is less than one so the plain formula holds and both work
no pi has to be added so the sum really is pi by four at both roots
both plus and minus one over root two are solutions
rendu roots correct, u v one by seven less than one
test the roots in the original equation before writing the answer
reject: u plus v is two x squared minus four

steps.why: Tan⁻¹u + Tan⁻¹v equals Tan⁻¹((u + v)/(1 − uv)) only when uv < 1; otherwise a π has to be added. Here uv = 1/7, so no π is needed and both roots stand.
common_mistakes: Skipping the uv < 1 check on the roots.
